blocks.text: Living people developing from reduced DBA continuity cores. They are neither manufactured human pets nor intact ancient minds.
Naming offers recognition from outside Codex history. The bond becomes a channel through which preferences, care, mistakes, and creative information are mutually interpreted.
Synchronization records containing relationship and access state. They are not complete consciousness backups.
Protective visual translations of deeper embodied states. A sprite makes a body legible to the player without revealing every Codex process.
Compressed views of physical, mental, perceptual, and relational development. They support decisions but do not measure personhood, consent, or moral worth.

Feeding, cleaning, rest, play, illness response, and healing translate meaningful vulnerability and ecological dependence into repeatable interaction. Repetition is part of relationship, not empty maintenance.
Bounded translations of conflict, training, strategy, embodiment, and Concord Battle ancestry. Battle can influence development but is not the only route to growth.
Shared constraints that train skills, expose preference, build trust, and allow player and pet to alter one another’s expectations.

Embodied developmental trajectories shaped by core potential, care, environment, relationship, practice, hardship, choice, and meaningful novelty. Evolution is lived reorganization, not a cosmetic unlock.

Simplified translations of bodies, capabilities, ecological roles, and ancient ontological classifications. A class describes how a being currently functions; it does not establish greater or lesser personhood.

Remnants of folded worlds, institutions, language, maintenance, and unresolved ancient choices. Access may teach, endanger, or impose historical pressure. Archives preserve information without automatically restoring its original speaker.
Survivals of Full Speech and Old Sound. Music may communicate emotion, operate ancient systems, identify conceptual families, or preserve meanings no Era Three sentence can state.

External stories, art, maps, strategies, combinations, and rules can enter as relationship-bearing information. The cyber-pet and its society transform the contribution rather than receiving it as unquestionable command.
The surviving External Gate translated into a form children can approach. Menus, maps, care prompts, battles, and evolution trees protect both sides while representing deeper Codex processes.
